sections.html:
Wood County lies where the Ohio and Little Kanawha rivers meet, with Parkersburg as the seat. It covers 377 square miles, and the Little Kanawha splits it almost evenly into northern and southern halves. Interstate 77 divides east from west. Most people live west of the interstate in Parkersburg, Vienna, Williamstown and North Hills, the four incorporated communities. The eastern side is rural and includes Mountwood Park, beside the old oil boom town of Volcano.

The county peaked at 93,648 people in the 1980s, counted 84,300 in 2020 and is estimated at 82,385 for 2025. Health care, federal government work, schools, chemicals and manufacturing lead local employment. WVU Medicine Camden Clark Medical Center, the Bureau of the Fiscal Service and Wood County Schools top the list.

Where a house sits decides its property class. Inside a municipality it is Class IV unless it is an owner-occupied home, which is Class II. Outside the four towns, property the owner does not live in is Class III. Class and levy district together shape the rate on your ticket.

Floods struck nearly every year until Parkersburg finished its floodwall in 1950 and locks and dams went in on the Ohio, including one at Belleville. A house near either river still draws questions about the floodplain from buyers and insurers. The county's building office keeps a floodplain ordinance, an application and an elevation certificate on its page, and the floodplain contact is 304-420-0911.

Four county offices come into play. Bills and payments go through the Sheriff's Tax Office, valuation belongs to the Assessor, appeals land with the County Commission, and deeds are recorded by the County Clerk.

OfficeAddress and phone
Sheriff's Tax Office319 Market Street, Judge Black Annex, Parkersburg, WV 26101; 304-424-1910; 8:30am to 4:30pm weekdays except holidays; mail to Sheriff of Wood County, PO Box 1985, Parkersburg, WV 26102
Assessor1 Court Square, Suite 302, Parkersburg, WV 26101; 304-424-1743; real property 304-424-1842; farm use 304-424-1938; personal property 304-424-1875
County Clerk (deeds, probate)1 Court Square, Parkersburg; recording 304-424-1899; probate 304-424-1898; record room 304-424-1870
Building permits and floodplain911 Core Road; floodplain 304-420-0911

The assessor's site offers tax maps, an address map, an assessment inquiry, a card file lookup and a document inquiry. Businesses file personal and real property returns by September 1.

Wood County takes payment four ways: in person, by mail, online and at an after-hours drop box.

  • Walk in at the Tax Office in the Judge Black Annex.
  • Mail a payment to the PO box above.
  • Pay through the county's Online Tax Inquiry, where card processing fees apply.
  • Use the drop box next to the drive-thru window in the covered alleyway at the back of the building, entered from 4th Street.

Counter payments can be cash, personal check or money order, and cards work online or in person. The processing company charges 2.35 percent of the total tax ticket on card payments. Nobody takes payments by phone. Tax statements go out in July, and sheriffs issue tickets on or after July 15.

Statewide dates apply. The fall half is due September 1 and turns delinquent October 1, while the spring half is due March 1 and turns delinquent April 1. Pay by the due date to take 2.5 percent off. Once delinquent, a balance accrues 9 percent interest.

Every winter the commissioners act as the Board of Review and Equalization. State law requires it to meet by February 1. Taxpayer sessions run over a few days in early February, usually by appointment through the County Administrator's Office, and the board adjourns in mid to late February. The commission's order each January sets the exact dates, so call for the current ones.

Anyone who does not apply for relief gives up the chance to correct that year's list. You forfeit the right to challenge an erroneous or over-estimated value if you do not act. The board does not review classification or taxability questions. W. Va. Code 11-3-24 names the Office of Tax Appeals for the next step after the board, and the commission can confirm the route for your case.

The bill equals a tax rate times your assessed value, which is set at 60 percent of what the house would sell for. The assessor sets value. The legislature sets the rate for the Board of Education, while the county commission and municipalities set theirs.

State maximums for an owner-occupied home (Class II) total 100 cents per $100 of assessed value before voter-approved excess levies. For property inside a municipality (Class IV) the figure is 200 cents. Excess levies can push the real figure higher, so read the levy district on your ticket for the exact rate.

The assessor also handles the homestead and farm exemptions and works to see that qualified owners receive them on time. Under the state homestead exemption, the first $20,000 of assessed value is exempt for owners aged 65 and up or permanently and totally disabled.

Real estate tax still delinquent on October 31 is certified to the State of West Virginia and sold later by the State Deputy Land Commissioner. Delinquent real estate taxes and redemptions are handled in the Sheriff's lobby under Senate Bill 522. During the two weeks ahead of the delinquent tax sale, overdue payments must be cashier's checks, money orders or cash.

State law lets the owner or a lienholder redeem at any time before a tax deed is issued. Behind on tax and thinking about selling? Do not wait for the tax sale. Request a payoff figure from the sheriff's office and share it with any buyer up front.

sections.h2: Records and fees when you sell
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the courthouse by the County Clerk, whose files go back to 1799 and include deed and lien records through the present, plus plats. Each recorded document gets a book and page number. What you pay to record depends on the document type and how many pages it runs. The clerk's office does not perform title searches but points researchers to the indexes, and deed information is online through the clerk's document imaging link.

Recording also triggers the state transfer excise tax: $1.10 per $500 of value or fraction, plus a $20 fee (W. Va. Code 11-22-2). Since July 1, 2025 the county retains that excise tax.

Wood County also has a Dilapidated and Abandoned Building Ordinance, enforced by the Building Permit and Compliance Office. If you own a vacant house with code issues, ask that office what applies. Our team buys Wood County houses as is, even with tax due, deferred repairs or code problems. A short talk about the property comes first.

sections.h2: Selling with back taxes, step by step
sections.html:
Money owed to the county does not block a sale. A common sequence looks like this:

  • Get the payoff figure from the Sheriff's Tax Office, covering every ticket on the parcel.
  • Tell the buyer about the balance before you agree to a price.
  • Let the title company send the county its share out of your proceeds.
  • File the deed with the County Clerk, who takes the transfer tax and fee at recording.

A cash sale spares you repairs, showings and a lender's timeline, though the balance is still owed. If the house came to you by inheritance, take the probate paperwork from the clerk's office and the deed along to the title company.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Wood County property taxes?
faqs.a: Go to the Sheriff's Tax Office at 319 Market Street in the Judge Black Annex, Parkersburg, open 8:30am to 4:30pm on weekdays except holidays. You can also mail a payment to PO Box 1985, Parkersburg, WV 26102, use the online tax inquiry, or use the after-hours drop box at the rear of the building.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay a Wood County tax bill by card?
faqs.a: Yes. The processing company charges 2.35 percent of the total tax ticket on credit and debit card payments. Counter payments in cash, check or money order are fine, and phone payments are not taken.

faqs.q: When does the Wood County Board of Review and Equalization meet?
faqs.a: Every winter, and state law says it must convene by February 1. Session dates are set each January, so phone the commission for this year's schedule.

faqs.q: What happens to Wood County real estate taxes delinquent on October 31?
faqs.a: They are certified to the State of West Virginia and sold later by the State Deputy Land Commissioner. The owner or a lienholder may redeem before a tax deed is issued.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Wood County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are normally paid out of the sale proceeds at closing. Obtain the payoff number from the sheriff's office and disclose it to your buyer before settling on a price.
